mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 5% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to persistent higher real borrowing costs compressing equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of high-rate periods, or FEDFUNDS drops below 5% within the next 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in hourly wage growth (implied via UNRATE) predicts negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns as weak labor demand suppresses corporate earnings growth.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases over the next month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive when labor indicators show this pattern, or wage growth outpaces unemployment rise.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) coinciding with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a demand-supply imbalance favoring S&P 500 gains in the near term (20 days).
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >10% while INDPRO decreases over the next month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative despite the pattern, or both proxies revert to trend within 5 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 50-week moving average predicts negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns due to contraction in manufacturing output.
failure_condition: INDPRO recovers above the 50-week MA within 3 days, and 5-day returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 3% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to market anticipation of rate hikes.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive when inflation crosses back below 3% within 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in unemployment (PAYEMS) below the prior month's level triggers a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as labor market tightening supports corporate optimism.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative or unchanged when PAYEMS remains flat or rises.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in both consumer (HOUST) and business investment demand indicators (implied via RSAFS) predict positive S&P 500 60-day returns as overall economic momentum strengthens.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are flat or negative despite both proxies rising in trend.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in manufacturing activity (INDPRO) over three consecutive months predicts negative S&P 500 20-day returns as market anticipates further supply-side weakness.
failure_condition: INDPRO recovers sharply within 10 days, and 20-day returns are positive.
